Rashi on Yevamot 42b:10:1.hebrew: מנקיט - מלקט ממנו הלכות פסוקות, הלכה כפלוני ופלוני:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:10:1.english: Gathers - He gathers from him decided halakhic rulings, [such as] "the halakha is in accordance with so-and-so and so-and-so."

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:1.hebrew: ואי מינסבא דלמא מיעברא - לאחר לידתה, ומיעכר עליה חלבה, וקטלה לברה ברעב:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:1.english: And if she marries, perhaps she will become pregnant - after she gives birth, and her milk will become spoiled upon her, and she will kill her son through starvation.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:2.english: She will feed [memasmesa] him - She gives him to eat.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:3.english: The husband will not give her - Because he is not his son.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:4.english: And let her sue the heirs - of the first husband.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:5.hebrew: אשה בושה לבא לב"ד - ולתבוע יורשים בשביל בנה:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:5.english: A woman is embarrassed to come to court - and to sue the heirs on behalf of her son.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:1:6.english: And she kills her son - Against her will, her son dies of hunger.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:2:1.hebrew: הי נינהו בתולות הי נינהו ארוסות - הא חדא היא, דהיכי משכחת לה בתולה יבמה אם לא ארוסה:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:2:1.english: Which are virgins [and] which are betrothed - [Surely] this is one [and the same], for how can you find a virgin levirate widow if not [one who was] betrothed?

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:3:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר - כלומר, לא תתני "אחת ואחת" דמשמע תרי מילי, אלא כולה חדא קתני, ופרושי קמפרש: אחת בתולות ואחת בעולות, וכגון שנתארמלו או נתגרשו, בין מן האירוסין — דהיינו בתולות — בין מן הנשואין — דהיינו בעולות:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:3:1.english: This is what it is saying - That is to say, do not teach "both [this] and [that]," which implies two [distinct] matters; rather, the entire [statement] teaches one [matter], and it is explaining [itself]: both virgins and non-virgins, and [specifically] in a case where they were widowed or divorced — whether from betrothal, which refers to virgins, or whether from marriage, which refers to non-virgins.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:4:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יוסי - דשרי ארוסות לינשא, הואיל וליכא למיחש לזרע ראשון, ונשואה ליארס. והאי דנקט ר' יוסי ולא רבי יהודה — דהא רבי יהודה נמי שרי ארוסה לינשא בהדיא — אלא משום דר' יוסי נימוקו עמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:4:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - Who permits betrothed women to marry, since there is no concern about the first [husband's] seed, and [permits] a married woman to become betrothed. And the reason [Rabbi Yoḥanan] mentioned Rabbi Yosei and not Rabbi Yehudah — for Rabbi Yehudah also explicitly permits a betrothed woman to marry — [is] rather because Rabbi Yosei's reasoning is with him.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:1.hebrew: מכלל דיחידאה פליג עליה - תנא קמא דאמר לא ינשאו ולא יתארסו אחת ארוסות ואחת בתולות — דאסר אפי' ארוסות ליארס, כ"ש לינשא — יחידאה היא, ולאו סתמא דרבים היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:1.english: From the fact that an individual disagrees with him - The first Tanna, who said, "They may not marry and they may not become betrothed, whether betrothed women or virgins" — for he forbade even betrothed women from becoming betrothed, [and] all the more so from marrying — is an individual [opinion], and is not an anonymous [teaching] of the majority.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:2.hebrew: ה"ג אין והתניא - בניחותא:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:2.english: This is the reading: "Yes, and it is taught" - [Read this] in a declarative tone [rather than as a question].

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:3.english: Pursued - Accustomed [to going there]. And furthermore, close to [her husband's] death she stayed in her father's house for a long time, so that one cannot say she is pregnant.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:5:4.english: Or that she had anger - and she did not have marital relations.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:6:1.english: Barren - [A woman] whose womb was uprooted and whose uterus was removed.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:6:2.hebrew: אילונית - ממעי אמה לקויה היא, ואין לה סימני שער ודדים:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:6:2.english: Aylonit - She is impaired from her mother's womb, and she has no signs of [pubic] hair or breasts.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:6:3.english: Or one who is unsuited to give birth - [This comes] to include [one who is unsuited] due to a potion or illness.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:6:4.english: All of them must wait - For they decreed [regarding] one who is unsuited [to give birth] on account of one who is suited [to give birth].

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:7:1.hebrew: ממתני' דכרמא - שנשנית בכרם ביבנה, מחמת אותה משנה חזר בו:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:7:1.english: From the baraita of the vineyard - Which was taught in the vineyard in Yavneh; because of that teaching, he retracted.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:7:2.english: In the vineyard in Yavneh - For they would sit [in] rows [upon] rows, like a vineyard.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:1.hebrew: לא חש לקימחיה - למה שהוא טוחן ומוציא מפיו, כלומר לדיבורו:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:1.english: [He] is not concerned for his flour - [That is,] for what he grinds and brings forth from his mouth, meaning, his words.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:2.hebrew: סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת היא - דהא איפלגו עלה ר' יוסי ור' יהודה:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:2.english: It is an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute - For Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Yehudah disputed regarding it.

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:3.hebrew: מחלוקת ואחר כך סתם - בין שסתם אחריה מיד באחד מהם, בין שסתם אחריה במסכת אחרת באותו הסדר — כגון נתן צמר לצבע, דמחלוקת בב"ק בהגוזל (ב"ק דף ק:), וסתם בב"מ (דף עו.): "כל המשנה ידו על התחתונה", וסתם לן כר"י דאמר "אם השבח יתר על היציאה כו'" — הלכה כסתם:
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:3.english: A dispute and afterward an unattributed [ruling] - Whether [the Mishna] stated an unattributed [ruling] immediately afterward in one of them [i.e., in the same tractate], or whether it stated an unattributed [ruling] afterward in another tractate in the same order — for example, [the case of] one who gave wool to a dyer, which is a dispute in Bava Kamma in [the chapter] HaGozel (Bava Kamma 100b), and is stated unattributed in Bava Metzia (76a): "Whoever changes [the terms of an agreement] has the lower hand," thus [the Mishna] taught us an unattributed [ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who says, "If the appreciation exceeds the expense, etc." — the halakha is in accordance with the unattributed [ruling].

Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:4.hebrew: סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת - כי מתני':
Rashi on Yevamot 42b:9:4.english: An unattributed [ruling] and afterward a dispute - Like our Mishnah.

Tosafot on Yevamot 42b:4:1.hebrew: הלכה כרבי יוסי - ול"ג כרבי יהודה, דהא בפ' מי שהוציאוהו (עירובין דף מו:) קאמר רבי יעקב בר אידי אמר רבי יוחנן: "רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה — הלכה כר"י; ר"י ורבי יוסי — הלכה כרבי יוסי; ואין צ"ל רבי מאיר ורבי יוסי — הלכה כרבי יוסי". ודייק דליתנהו להני כללי מדאיצטריך רבי יוחנן לפסוק כרבי יוסי אף על גב דיחידאה פליג עליה; ואי גרס "הלכה כרבי יהודה", שפיר איצטריך לפסוק הלכה כר' יהודה לאפוקי מר' יוסי דפליג עליה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 42b:4:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - And we do not read [the text as] "in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah", for in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (Eruvin 46b), Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said [that] Rabbi Yochanan said: "Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah — the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah; Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Yosei — the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei; and it goes without saying [regarding] Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei." And [the Gemara] infers that these rules do not apply, since Rabbi Yochanan needed to rule in accordance with Rabbi Yosei even though [only] an individual disagrees with him; whereas if one were to read "the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah", it would rightly be necessary to rule that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehudah, to exclude [the opinion of] Rabbi Yosei who disagrees with him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 42b:9:1.hebrew: סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת היא - וא"ת: והא אמרינן בריש מסכת ביצה (דף ב.) גבי שבת: "סתם לן תנא כר"ש", דתנן: "מחתכין הדלועין כו'", אע"ג דפליג ר' יהודה בסיפא וקאמר: "אם לא היתה נבילה מערב שבת כו'"? ויש לומר: דנהי דלא חשיב סתם גמור, מ"מ חשיב כרבים לגבי יחיד. וא"ת: בפ' המוציא יין (שבת פא: ושם) דפריך: "ומי סבר רבי יוחנן דבר שאין מתכוין אסור? והאמר ר' יוחנן: הלכה כסתם משנה, ותנן: נזיר חופף ומפספס אבל לא סורק!", ומאי קושיא? דסתמא בנזיר (דף מב.) ופלוגתא בפ"ב דביצה (דף כג.) גבי קירוד וקרצוף, ובתרי מסכתי אמר בפ"ק דמס' ע"ז (דף ז. ושם): "אין סדר למשנה"! וליכא למימר דר' יוחנן אית ליה הלכה כסתם אפי' בסתם ואח"כ מחלוקת, דהא קאמר הכא בהדיא אליבא דר' יוחנן: "סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת היא"! וי"ל: דודאי בסתם ואח"כ מחלוקת מודה ר' יוחנן דאין הלכה כסתם, אבל בתרי מסכתי אית ליה לר' יוחנן דהלכתא כסתם. וטעמא דר' יוחנן — משום דמסתמא אית לן למימר דמחלוקת ואח"כ סתם הוא, ולא סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת, דאין לנו לומר שחזר בו רבי מפסקו עד שנראה בפירוש. ומיהו שאר אמוראי אית להו דבתרי מסכתי אין סדר למשנה, ואין הלכתא כסתם. וא"ת: דבפ' כל גגות (עירובין דף צב. ושם) פסק ר' יוחנן כר"ש בין עירבו בין לא עירבו, ופריך: "והא אמר ר' יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה", ומייתי מסתם משנה דבפרק חלון (עירובין דף עו:) — והיינו סתם ואח"כ מחלוקת? ותירץ ה"ר אהרן כהן: דעיקר קושיא לרבי יוחנן אינה אלא דלא גזר בעירבו; ובזה הדבר הוי מחלוקת ואח"כ סתם — מחלוקת בשלש חצירות במי שהוציאוהו (שם דף מה:), וסתם בפרק חלון, אבל בפרק כל גגות לא פליגי בגזירה. ומיהו קשה: דבסוף פרק קמא דמסכת ע"ז (דף כא.) גבי שכירות בתים, פסק שמואל כרבי יוסי אע"ג דסתם לן תנא בתר הכי כרבי מאיר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 42b:9:1.english: It is an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute - And if you ask: Do we not say at the beginning of Tractate Beitzah (2a) regarding Shabbat [that] the Tanna taught us an unattributed [ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, as we learned in the Mishnah: "One may cut up gourds, etc.," even though Rabbi Yehudah disagrees in the latter clause and says: "If it was not already a carcass before Shabbat, etc."? One can answer that even though it is not considered a complete unattributed [ruling], nevertheless it is considered like a majority against an individual. And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Hamotzi Yayin (Shabbat 81b and thereabouts), where [the Gemara] asks: "Does Rabbi Yochanan really hold that an unintended act is forbidden? Did not Rabbi Yochanan say: The halakha is in accordance with an unattributed Mishnah, and we learned in a Mishnah: A nazirite may wash [his hair] and part [it with his fingers], but he may not comb [it]!" — what is the difficulty? For the unattributed [Mishnah] is in Nazir (42a) and the dispute is in the second chapter of Beitzah (23a) regarding scraping and currying, and in two [different] tractates [the Gemara] said in the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (7a and thereabouts): "There is no [chronological] order to the Mishnah"! And one cannot say that Rabbi Yochanan holds that the halakha is in accordance with an unattributed [ruling] even in [a case of] an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute, for here [the Gemara] explicitly says according to Rabbi Yochanan: "It is an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute"! One can answer that certainly in [a case of] an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute, Rabbi Yochanan concedes that the halakha is not in accordance with the unattributed [ruling]; however, in two [different] tractates, Rabbi Yochanan holds that the halakha is in accordance with the unattributed [ruling]. And Rabbi Yochanan's reason is because presumably we should say that it is a dispute followed by an unattributed [ruling], and not an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute — for we should not say that Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi] retracted his ruling until we see [so] explicitly. However, the other Amoraim hold that in two [different] tractates there is no [chronological] order to the Mishnah, and the halakha is not in accordance with the unattributed [ruling]. And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot (Eruvin 92a and thereabouts), Rabbi Yochanan ruled in accordance with Rabbi Shimon whether they made an eruv or whether they did not make an eruv, and [the Gemara] asks: "Did not Rabbi Yochanan say: The halakha is in accordance with an unattributed Mishnah," and brings [a proof] from the unattributed Mishnah in the chapter [entitled] Chalon (Eruvin 76b) — and that is an unattributed [ruling] followed by a dispute? And Rabbi Aharon Kohen answered that the primary difficulty for Rabbi Yochanan is only that he did not make a [rabbinic] decree when they made an eruv; and regarding this matter it is a dispute followed by an unattributed [ruling] — a dispute regarding three courtyards in [the chapter] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (ibid. 45b), and an unattributed [ruling] in the chapter [entitled] Chalon — whereas in the chapter [entitled] Kol Gagot they do not disagree about the decree. However, it is difficult, for at the end of the first chapter of Tractate Avodah Zarah (21a) regarding the renting of houses, Shmuel ruled in accordance with Rabbi Yose even though the Tanna taught us an unattributed [ruling] afterward in accordance with Rabbi Meir:
